summary: State-built tower on Beaver Lick Mountain, transferred to the Monongahela in 1948, last staffed 1973; firelookout.org index lists it as gone.

facts.design: all-metal cab on a short steel tower about 25 feet tall
facts.status_note: firelookout.org index lists it as Tower Gone; no removal date found

events.note: Tower on Beaver Lick Mountain noted as served by the Marlinton central office (Charleston Gazette item)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts calls it Beaver Lick Mountain (White Rock); the FFLOS record and the index use Beaver Lick (White Rocks). Both name the same tower site.

sources.title: Fire Towers: Fifty Years of Early Detection and Fire Protection

notes_for_editor: Transfer to the Monongahela (1948) and 2017 registration are well supported. No built year appears in the sources; the 1926 Gazette item mentions a tower on Beaver Lick Mountain, which may be the state tower but is not confirmed. Removal date not found; the index is the only source saying Tower Gone. No access or present-condition information found. No photos added. Brief record matched on coordinates, elevation, agency and 2017 registration; no corrections proposed.
